findings.title: Codex response filename is bound to jq's input operand
findings.observation: Cycle 8 parses supported jq flags and option arity before identifying the filter and positional inputs. The singular shape requires exactly one positional input equal to the successful response file; the array shape requires null input, zero positionals and one exact --slurpfile binding referenced by the selector.
findings.trigger: Replay the prior --arg marker replay-response.json counterexample and adjacent malformed/ambiguous input-role variants against the exact-head verifier.
findings.impact: The prior false compatibility record is rejected while legitimate direct and --slurpfile readers remain accepted, restoring the AC-15 response-to-claim correlation gate.

evidence.description: The committed Cycle 7 counterexample now rejects when replay-response.json is only a --arg value and unrelated-replay-response.json is the positional input.
parseJqInvocation separates jq option values from filter and positional inputs, rejecting unknown or malformed options.
responseReaderShape proves the exact direct positional input or one selector-bound exact --slurpfile binding before exposing any parsed output.
Supported direct readers with unrelated option values and supported null-input --slurpfile readers pass; alias, command-boundary and option-value substitutions fail.
Reviewer-added multiple-positional, --rawfile substitution, duplicate exact --slurpfile and unknown-option negatives all failed closed; real Codex and Claude proof replays passed.
AC-15 requires each named client to actually execute the representative validation, and the plan disallows a hand-written assertion without live request/resource correlation.

findings.remediation: Completed at the current head: supported jq invocation roles are parsed and exact input identity is required.
findings.verification: Both real client records pass; all existing negatives remain closed; the routed --arg/positional-input case and reviewer-added malformed/ambiguous variants fail with CLIENT_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED_TRANSCRIPT.

findings.title: Child-resource writes are committed without matching public reads
findings.observation: The current implementation maps every scenario result ref to a direct or paginated public read and requires an exact ID match.
findings.trigger: A normal, recovered or terminal-replayed journal entry contains a child resource reference.
findings.impact: The exact child must be publicly present before COMMITTED/PASS; missing or mismatched children now fail closed.

evidence.description: Exact report/progress reads pass, mismatched progress fails, and terminal replay performs zero writes while reading reports and progress.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI verify normal, recovery and terminal readback behavior.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS is persisted as terminal rejection
findings.observation: The current recovery helper recognizes the bounded retry contract, preserves exact bytes/key and leaves exhaustion OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
findings.trigger: Recovery receives one or more 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS responses.
findings.impact: Temporary concurrency no longer becomes terminal local rejection and the original intent remains resumable.

evidence.description: The exact-head regression proves retry-success after two sends and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN after three bounded in-progress responses, with identical body and key.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI pass.
